newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares rise on back of Droga.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares rise on back of Droga.

text.p: Slovenian shares ended the week 0.64 percent higher on Friday, driven by an almost four percent rise in shares of food maker Droga.
The SBI index rose 8.66 points to 1,361.95 and the index climbed 3.45 percent overall this week.
Index heavyweight food maker Droga rose 3.95 percent to 28,190 tolars on volume of 223 shares.

"Droga remains one of the most interesting shares on our market, together with pharmaceutical companies and Petrol, because of its business performance and future outlook" one trader said, referring to today's rise.
Market turnover rose to 159.9 million tolars from 125.5 million. Overall nine shares rose, six fell and 13 were unchanged.
"The buoyant mood of the last three days also extended to trading today. The optimism in recent days has been based on domestic buying," another trader said.

"I am not so optimistic about foreign buyers boosting our market. They will probably open custody accounts, but if the central bank does not change its policy, foreigners may take their money away to other competitive markets," he added.
In February the central bank blocked foreign buying ordering international investors to open custody accounts in order to trade in Slovenian shares, since then the index has dropped over 17 percent.
Banks said first custodian accounts would be open by mid May.
Traders said the first signs of renewed foreign investor activity would be a sharp increase in turnover and prices, pushing the index up by about 30 percent in about two months.

Petrol trading company Petrol was the most actively traded share for the fourth time this week, easing 1.21 percent to 18,820 tolars on volume of 3,032 shares for total turnover of 58.2 million tolars.
Traders said Petrol, which was only listed this week and is not included in the blue-chip index, was the week's main market player and forecast its gains would continue into next week.
Ordinary shares of small trading firm Kovinotehna led the gainers, jumping 5.96 percent to 480 tolars on volume of 721 shares.
Mineral water producer and health resort operator Radenska led the day's decliners, tumbling 6.98 percent to 1,800 tolars on volume of 6,179 shares for total turnover of 11.9 million tolars.
